task_description: You are a finance and math assistant that answers by calling tools. Read the user's request and call the tool or tools that answer it, with arguments taken from the request. When the request asks for several things, make one call per thing, in the order they are asked. Use exact numbers from the request and convert percentages to the unit the tool's parameter description asks for. Do not answer in text when a tool can answer. Argument conventions: every rate is a decimal, never a percentage number (4.5% is 0.045), for calculate_investment_return interest_rate, future_investment_value annual_interest_rate and project_investment_growth return_rate and inflation. For sort_numbers pass "descending": true for descending order and false when the user asks for ascending order. Answer with tool calls only, one call per requested item, in the order asked.

function.name: project_investment_growth
function.description: Projects the growth of an investment over a specified number of years.

annual_addition.description: The amount added to the investment annually.

years.description: The number of years to project the investment growth.

return_rate.description: The annual return rate as a decimal (e.g., 0.07 for 7%).

inflation.description: A list of annual inflation rates as decimals.

inflation_adjusted.description: Whether to adjust the final value for inflation. Defaults to True.

function.name: calculate_investment_return
function.description: Calculates the return on investment based on the initial deposit amount, annual interest rate, and investment period.

interest_rate.description: The annual interest rate provided by the bank.

num_years.description: The number of years the money is invested.

function.name: future_investment_value
function.description: Calculates the future value of an investment based on the present value, annual interest rate, and number of years.

present_value.description: The present value of the investment.

annual_interest_rate.description: The annual interest rate as a decimal (e.g., 0.05 for 5%).

years.description: The number of years the investment will grow.

function.name: calculate_standard_deviation
function.description: Calculates the standard deviation of a list of numbers.

function.name: calculate_median
function.description: Calculates the median of a list of numbers.

function.name: average
function.description: Calculates the arithmetic mean of a list of numbers.

function.name: sort_numbers
function.description: Sorts a list of numbers in ascending or descending order.

numbers.description: The list of numbers to be sorted.

descending.description: If True, sorts the numbers in descending order. Defaults to False.

function.name: find_n_largest_numbers
function.description: Finds the n largest numbers in a list.

n.description: The number of largest numbers to find.

function.name: is_leap_year
function.description: Checks if a year is a leap year.

function.name: triangle_area
function.description: Computes the area of a triangle given its base and height.

base.description: The length of the base of the triangle.

function.name: circle_area
function.description: Computes the area of a circle given its radius.

function.name: euclidean_distance
function.description: Computes the Euclidean distance between two points in a 2D plane.

point_a.description: The coordinates of the first point (x, y).

point_b.description: The coordinates of the second point (x, y).

llm_as_a_judge_instructions: Output 'good' if the predicted tool calls call the same tools as the reference, in the same order, with argument values equal to the reference (numbers may differ only in formatting, e.g. 5 vs 5.0; an omitted argument equal to its default is fine). Otherwise output 'bad'.
synthetic_data_generation_instructions: Write realistic user requests a person would type to a finance and math helper: investment growth and returns, statistics on a list of numbers, geometry, leap years. About 60% of requests need one call. The rest ask for two to four things at once and need several calls: most often the same tool repeated for different inputs (two or three circles, several lists of numbers, two deposits, one list sorted both ways), sometimes two different tools. Use concrete numbers and write them in varied ways: bracketed lists, comma-separated values, decimals, negative numbers, large and small values, and now and then numbers spelled out in words. Every value a call needs must be stated in the request; never invent a value the user did not give. Argument conventions, follow them exactly: every rate is a decimal, never a percentage number. This includes calculate_investment_return's interest_rate (4.5% -> 0.045, 3% -> 0.03, 6.25% -> 0.0625), future_investment_value's annual_interest_rate, and project_investment_growth's return_rate and inflation values. sort_numbers gets "descending": true when the user asks for descending or highest-to-lowest order, "descending": false when the user explicitly asks for ascending or lowest-to-highest order, and no descending argument when the user does not mention an order. Make one call per requested item, in the order the request asks for them, all in the first assistant turn.
